analysis.title: Sunday Start | What's Next in Global Macro: Embracing Risk, Not Ignoring It
key_insights: Morgan Stanley is constructive on growth. US growth is driven by AI capex and household spending, and AI-driven wealth supports consumption. Less conviction in AI would mean less confidence in overall growth.

Asia Pacific Summit clients pushed back on the Strategy title 'Embracing Risk', given MS Research's overweight equity recommendations globally. Equities continued to sell off on Friday after the conference.
The Asian capex cycle is seen as broadening and becoming self-sustaining beyond AI, while US capex fuels exports from Asia.
Inflation is the lower-conviction forecast. MS expects a peak in Q1 2027 and a gradual retreat, so DM central banks hike less than markets price.

If inflation surprises, upside is more likely than downside. An energy shock plus tighter policy causing a growth slump is risk negative, but demand-driven inflation with pricing power would be positive for equities.
The path to end-2027 is expected to be non-linear. Even one-off upside inflation surprises could trigger further repricing of policy expectations and higher rates.
Fiscal risks are likely to grow, including a possible US shutdown or debt limit episode and elections worldwide, especially France where the fiscal path has moved sovereign debt markets.
The message is 'embrace risk', not 'relax, the worst is over'. MS strategists present bull and bear cases and economists present upside and downside scenarios.
US PCE for October (due 11/25): MS expects core PCE +0.30% m/m (3.2% y/y) and headline +0.33% m/m (3.8% y/y), with core goods accelerating on energy and shipping pass-through.
Other US data this week: real spending +0.1% m/m, saving rate 3.7%, new home sales 640k (-5.3% m/m), and the goods trade deficit narrowing to $130.0bn.
Central bank calendar: BoK expected to hike 25bp on 26 Nov with the dot plot upper level possibly at 3.75%. Israel BOI is expected on hold, with a chance of a cut to 3%.
Lower energy prices are expected to lift euro area and German sentiment: euro area composite PMI forecast 52.0, ifo 90.5, economic confidence 97.2.

sector_views.rationale: MS Research has overweight recommendations on equities globally, based on solid growth and inflation unlikely to derail the trend.

tension_points.bull_case: Growth stays solid on AI capex and household spending, and demand-driven inflation with pricing power would support nominal earnings.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky inflation from an energy shock plus tighter policy could cause a growth slump, and clients pushed back with equities selling off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation surprises that drive further recalibration of policy expectations and higher rates, or weaker conviction in the AI story.

theme_stances.key_argument: The vast majority of evidence says growth stays solid and sticky inflation probably will not derail the trend.
theme_stances.evidence: we are saying “embrace risk,” not “relax, the worst is over.”

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation is expected to peak in Q1 and DM central banks should hike less than priced.
theme_stances.evidence: DM central banks will hike rates less than what is currently priced in markets.
